clue.text: A line enclosed by youth leader on "Austerity"

parts.note: a line is a string or cord
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, as written at the foot of a letter

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A youth leader takes a line on the theme of austerity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' looks like a container signal, but it is the letter-writer's abbreviation ENC. 'on' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringency is severity or harshness of manner, so it is a synonym for austerity.

clue.text: Thirteens, at this stage, are out of order!

definitions.text: Thirteens, at this stage, are out of order!

parts.words: Thirteens, at this stage, are out of order!
parts.note: thirteen split as a six and a seven, in the plural, is the idiom for chaos and disorder

explanation.surface: An official complains that the number thirteens are jumbled at this point.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in total confusion, and six plus seven makes thirteen.

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, the game
an editor, ED, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A sports reporter wishes he had not covered the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to be sorry for it, so the past tense means felt sorry about.

indicators.note: reproduced suggests the letters are made again in a new form

explanation.surface: A recording of Leo comes out with a lumpy sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' rearranges the letters of SOUND and LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulose describes something covered in small knots or nodules, hence knobbly.

clue.text: At last I have some salad

parts.note: at last means in the end
contracted, I have is I've

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets a share of the salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory plant eaten raw in a green dish.

clue.text: About to put down the earth

parts.note: C stands for circa, about
to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Someone is about to set something down on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a kind of soil, so it is earth in the gardener's sense.

clue.text: Leaning tower perhaps, one protected from being knocked down

definitions.text: one protected from being knocked down

explanation.surface: The Leaning Tower is a structure saved from demolition.
explanation.walkthrough: A leaning tower is one that lists, so it is cryptically a building that is listed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilting tower is a structure that lists; a building under heritage protection may not be demolished.

clue.text: Attractive as a hook should be?

definitions.text: Attractive as a hook should be?

parts.words: Attractive as a hook should be?
parts.note: on a dress fastening a hook is meant to latch onto its partner loop, read as a phrase about grabbing attention

explanation.surface: A tailor wants the hooks on a dress to look striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that grabs the gaze is striking, and a hook literally engages the matching loop of a fastening.

parts.note: relatively is read as made up of relatives, a big set of kin

explanation.surface: A fairly big gathering of people.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means all one's relations beyond parents and children, such as aunts and cousins.

parts.note: a common is public parkland
a place is an area or spot

explanation.surface: Is a park just an everyday sort of area?
explanation.definitionFit: Something commonplace is mundane and unremarkable.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for mud is spoken, giving the river's sound

parts.note: ooze is soft mud

explanation.surface: A river full of mud.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in England; OOZE spoken sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, one flowing through York.

parts.note: on hand reads as worn over the hand, and fitting as snugly sized

explanation.surface: It is fitting to have it on hand, meaning available.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand covering of fabric or leather is worn snugly on the hand.

clue.text: Pedro tickled part of the ear

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective meaning relating to this noun

indicators.note: part of signals that the letters come from within the words Pedro tickled

explanation.surface: Pedro tickled someone's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective for things concerning the organ of hearing.

explanation.surface: A gift given as part of a store's marketing campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To present is to proffer something; a special deal in a shop is also called this.

clue.text: Graduate takes the one over here, leaving one school subject

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts graduate

indicators.note: leaving means the following letter departs from the word

parts.note: the one over here is this one
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A graduate grabs the one nearby and leaves a single school subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving one' drops the I from THIS to give THS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics, shortened in British usage, is a subject taught in class.

clue.text: It is obvious there is no end to the political propaganda

indicators.note: no end to means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a manifesto is a party's published programme of promises

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that political propaganda never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end to' removes the last O of MANIFESTO. 'no end' tempts as 'endless', a definition; it is the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plain to see, clear or evident.

clue.text: Outlaw put a stop to it, it was reported

indicators.note: reported signals the words are heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to ban it is to put a stop to it

explanation.surface: Police stopped an outlaw, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber who lives outside the law.

explanation.surface: The upper part of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Superior is the largest of North America's Great Lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior means higher in position; it is also one of the Great Lakes.

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone resents a confounded bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nester is a bird that builds a nest, an apt crossword term for a nesting bird.

indicators.note: repeated means the word is given twice in succession

parts.note: hush means silence

explanation.surface: Something was kept secret amid repeated calls for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush means confidential, highly classified.

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to clip is to cut
Che Guevara was the famous revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary idea gets cut short for being stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of CLIP, giving CLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is a worn-out, overused notion or expression.

explanation.surface: Be on stage right now.
explanation.definitionFit: To live is to exist; a concert broadcast as it happens is said to be on air in real time.

indicators.note: in places the general inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A general stands out in the street during a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleet is a mix of rain and snow falling from clouds.

clue.text: Evident one is not in eluded in the project

indicators.note: is not included means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: plain means evident
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Clearly one person has not been included in the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not included' drops the I from PLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or proposed undertaking.

indicators.note: re-read suggests the letters are read again in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone re-reads a racy passage in a science fiction novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-read' rearranges NUDE. Frank Herbert wrote the science fiction novel set on the desert planet Arrakis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dune is the 1965 science fiction novel by Frank Herbert.

explanation.surface: Someone fell down.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs. A fell is a northern English hill, and the downs are rolling chalk uplands of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell and a down are both regional British words for upland ground or a rise.

clue.text: Almost closely united with it is the eye inflammation

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: conjunctive means joined or closely united
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye inflammation is almost bound up with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' removes the last E of CONJUNCTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the membrane lining the eyelid, often called pink eye.

clue.text: Science met in its shortened form

explanation.surface: Someone met a science in a shortened form.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the British Met Office, and met is the standard short form of the weather science.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the science of weather and climate, abbreviated as met.
